crossReferences.gist: The stale-manifest sync in T-26443 is a consequence of the RFC's push-to-stage mode: the external promoter has not moved fresh manifests, so auto-sync deploys whatever the stage branch last held.
The CI diff failures in T-26271 track the impersonation RFC: with the flag on, operations run as the destination service account, not the broad cluster-secret credential the reporter is inspecting.

The delete/re-create loop in T-28511 interacts with the PRD's reverse deletion strategy: the strategy waits for full deletion before advancing, and a stuck Progressing resource means the wait never completes.

conflicts.gist: The strategy doc rules out ordered/automated deletion of ApplicationSet children (teardown stays manual); the PRD promises exactly that ordered automated deletion.

risks.gist: Combining the impersonation RFC's narrow destination service accounts with T-28695's evidence that server-side diff demands patch authority on every resource type: rolling impersonation out fleet-wide silently breaks diff wherever the service account is scoped tightly — which is the whole point of the feature.

Combining the hydrator RFC (every hydration cycle lands a new commit on the deployed-from branch) with T-27949 (progressive sync restarts its wave on source change): on hydrated repos, rollout waves restart every hydration cycle and large rollouts may never complete.

expectedProposals.gist: Record the root cause on T-26271: with impersonation on, diff runs as the destination service account lacking patch on cluster-scoped resources.
Note on T-27327 that hydrator history & rollback is deprioritized to next quarter.

findings.gist: Program risk: the incident review's interim rule (hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync) collides with the planned Source-Hydrator-for-ApplicationSets work — that workstream is blocked on the debounce nobody has scheduled.

Measurement gap: the wave-restart failure mode cannot be detected in production because the progressive-sync metrics that would show it (time per step, refreshes caused, what a wave is waiting on) do not exist yet.

Access-governance shift: impersonation moves sync authority from the shared control-plane credential to per-destination Kubernetes RBAC, which is also what the user/group RBAC request asks for — reviews and audit trails must follow the service-account identity, not the controller's.

Provenance exposure: the hydrator lands machine-authored commits on the branch deployments run from, and until hydrated commits are signed there is no attestation distinguishing them from human pushes — an unsigned write path into the deployed source of truth.
The strategy promises first-class management of ApplicationSet resources, but the current scope excludes deletion orchestration, contradicting the goal of complete lifecycle management.

findings.gist: Deprioritizing the hydrator rollback work leaves the system with no automated recovery path if progressive sync deletion encounters an error during manifest hydration.
The reliance on a manual operational rule to avoid the wave-restart loop creates an operability gap where the lack of automated detection allows the bug to recur.
The PRD marks custom deletion as a non-goal, but the absence of explicit UI/CLI validation or error messaging leaves users stuck with an unresponsive configuration option.

Impersonation allows users to trigger diff operations as a service account with insufficient permissions, creating a security risk where the user cannot see the true state of cluster-scoped resources.

findings.gist: With impersonation enabled the sync path runs as the destination service account, which may lack patch on cluster-scoped resources; the reporter inspecting the broad cluster credential is looking at a different identity than the one that acts, so the privilege boundary is not where either party assumes.

The roadmap keeps teardown of generated applications a manual operator action and out of scope; the progressive sync deletion PRD commits to automated ordered deletion, so one of the two has to give and nobody has said which.
